analysis.title: USA: FOMC Leaves Fed Funds Rate Unchanged; Cook and Hammack Dissent Preferring a 25bp Hike
key_insights: The FOMC held the fed funds target range at 3.75-4.00% at its October 2026 meeting, following a 25bp hike at the September meeting.
Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented, both preferring a 25bp hike. Hammack had also dissented in favor of a 25bp hike at the July meeting.

The statement kept the language that inflation 'remains elevated' and said 'the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal.'
The Committee upgraded its description of economic activity to expanding at a 'strong' pace, from 'solid' in September. The rest of the statement was unchanged from September.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Rates were held after the September 25bp hike. Two dissents in favor of a further 25bp hike show a hawkish minority on the Committee.

macro_indicators.reading: 2 dissents (Cook, Hammack), both preferring a 25bp hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: Both dissents leaned hawkish. Hammack also dissented in July, so the hike preference is a repeat for her.

macro_indicators.indicator: Economic activity characterization in FOMC statement
macro_indicators.interpretation: The upgrade in the activity description comes alongside statement language that inflation remains elevated.

risk_factors: Inflation 'remains elevated,' and the Committee says it needs more information to set the policy stance that returns inflation to 2 percent in a timely way.
